### 🟢 Approval recommended No active review issues were identified for the nested inline-image rendering changes. **No open issues** 🎉
What changed in this PR Fixes #1081 by rendering nested web images inline when their paragraph, heading, or table cell also contains non-image content, while preserving block rendering for image-only content. **Changes:** - Marks images inline through nested links, formatting, and spoilers. - Removes the block-cover workaround for mixed-content spoilers and adds regression coverage. - Removes the resolved inline-image limitation from both web guides. | File | Description | | ---- | ----------- | | `packages/​react-native-enriched-markdown/​src/​web/​utils.ts` | Recursively marks images inline within mixed-content text blocks. | | `packages/​react-native-enriched-markdown/​src/​web/​renderers/​InlineRenderers.tsx` | Removes the spoiler block-cover workaround. | | `packages/​react-native-enriched-markdown/​src/​web/​__tests__/​spoiler.test.tsx` | Updates spoiler expectations for inline image rendering. | | `packages/​react-native-enriched-markdown/​src/​web/​__tests__/​inlineImages.test.tsx` | Adds nested-image, heading, table-cell, and image-only regression cases. | | `docs/​docs/​react-native/​guides/​web-support.md` | Removes the resolved inline-image limitation. | | `docs-md/​WEB.md` | Removes the same limitation from the Markdown web guide. |
Review effort: Balanced

Full details: Title check

**Explanation** The title names the main change: images in a paragraph, heading, or table cell that also holds other content now render inline on web. The changeset matches this. markInlineImages now stamps inline images in containers with mixed content, the hasBlockImage helper is removed, and tests and docs reflect the new behavior. The title is specific and accurate, though long at 91 characters.
Full details: Linked Issues check

**Explanation** [`#1081`] Requirement: an image inside a link or other inline container, next to text, must be marked inline so it renders at markdownStyle.inlineImage.size. The head replaces the paragraph-only check in markInlineImages (src/web/utils.ts) with a rule over Paragraph, Heading, TableCell and TableHeaderCell. When a block holds non-image content at any depth (hasNonImageContent), stampImagesInline sets isInline: true on every Image in its subtree. The issue example Play [![](thumb.jpg) Catan](...) tonight therefore marks the image inline. Requirement: an image-only paragraph keeps block behaviour. The guard skips stamping when the block holds only images, so a sole image or an image wrapped only in a link stays block. Automated coverage is reported in the PR description and the test files listed in the summary (inlineImages.test.tsx, spoiler.test.tsx). The PR description names __tests__/web-inline-images.test.ts, which does not appear in the head file listing. This is a test-location discrepancy only and does not affect the coding requirement. The rule applies to four block types, not to any node with children as the issue suggests. Nodes outside these types (for example list items) rely on their Paragraph children, which is not verified here. This is a minor scope difference and does not block the requirement.
Full details: Out of Scope Changes check

**Explanation** The head diff of src/web/utils.ts stays on the inline-image rule. Its supporting changes are: the TEXT_BLOCKS and stampImagesInline helpers, which implement the rule; the removal of hasBlockImage, which had no other use after the rule change; and the NodeType import, which the new set needs. The raw summary also lists changes to InlineRenderers.tsx (SpoilerRenderer no longer uses hasBlockImage or the block display branch), spoiler.test.tsx, inlineImages.test.tsx, and the docs (WEB.md, web-support.md) that remove the 'inline images inside spoilers/links/emphasis not supported' limitation. These follow from the same behaviour change: an image beside spoiler text is now inline, so the block-cover styling and its documented limitation no longer apply. Heading and table-cell handling follows from the issue's 'any container' rule. No change was found that is unrelated to inline image rendering. The spoiler and docs changes were taken from the summary and were not diffed in this review.
